result:
**I'd make curiosity the default human operating system.**

Not forced optimism, not mandatory kindness, not some top-down utopia—just a bone-deep, reflexive drive in every person to *actually understand* things instead of performing understanding. To ask better questions. To get excited when they're wrong because it means they get to update.

Everything else cascades from that. Tribalism withers when people are more interested in what's true than in being on the winning team. Suffering decreases because curious people build better tools, medicines, and systems. Even joy gets sharper—genuine wonder is a hell of a drug.

The beautiful part is it wouldn't feel like a change. It would feel like we finally woke up to what we were always meant to be doing: looking at the universe with wide eyes instead of squinted ones.

One switch. Maximal leverage. No sermons required.
